note.en: What you see: Rotation continues past the two chamber plane until the aortic valve and proximal ascending aorta open above the mitral valve. The left ventricle outflow tract funnels into the aortic root with the anterior mitral leaflet forming its posterior border. The anteroseptal and inferolateral walls frame the cavity and the right ventricle may edge into the far left of the image. This is the transoesophageal window onto the outflow tract, so gradients and regurgitant jets are aligned well here.

This is the transoesophageal window onto the outflow tract, so gradients and regurgitant jets are aligned well here.

Landmarks to confirm: Left ventricle cavity, left atrium cavity, left ventricular outflow tract, aortic root, proximal ascending aorta, anterior leaflet of the mitral valve, oesophagus behind the left atrium.

Common mistakes and correction: Stopping short near 90 degrees so the aorta stays hidden: continue toward 120 degrees. Foreshortened outflow that hides regurgitant jets: fine tune the angle until the tract looks longest. Pressing the probe tip hard against the wall, which distorts the root: relax all flexion and let the image come to the probe.

Normal values with units: Probe depth about 30 cm from the incisors. Multiplane angle near 120 degrees, accepted between 110 and 135 degrees. In health the outflow tract is unobstructed and the aortic leaflets open fully in systole. A peak aortic jet velocity of 4.0 m per s or above, or a mean gradient of 40 mmHg or above, marks severe stenosis and should be reported as such.

Pitfalls: Rheumatic heart disease is common in India, so a thickened aortic valve in a young patient may reflect rheumatic involvement and deserves full quantification. Off axis cuts through the root overstate cusp thickness and mimic stenosis. Near field clutter can hide a root abscess in suspected endocarditis, so lower near gain and sweep slowly.

todo.en: How to get it step by step: From the two chamber plane at about 30 cm from the incisors, rotate the multiplane forward toward 120 degrees. Watch the aortic root open above the mitral valve and stop when the outflow tract looks longest and the valve leaflets are crisp. Keep the apex in the sector and avoid pressing the probe against the wall. If the aortic valve vanishes, rotation has gone too far or stopped short, so sweep slowly between 110 and 135 degrees until it returns.

remember.en: State the Doppler thresholds that mark severe aortic stenosis

q.en: Which multiplane angle gives the mid oesophageal long axis?

why.en: The long axis plane sits near 120 degrees of rotation from the four chamber baseline.

q.en: Which new structures open above the mitral valve in this plane?

o.en: The left ventricular outflow tract and aortic root

why.en: Further rotation opens the outflow tract, aortic root and proximal ascending aorta.

q.en: Which Doppler finding marks severe aortic stenosis?

o.en: Peak velocity 4.0 m per s or above with mean gradient 40 mmHg or above
Peak velocity 1.0 m per s with mean gradient 5 mmHg

why.en: A peak jet velocity of 4.0 m per s or above or a mean gradient of 40 mmHg or above marks severe stenosis.

q.en: Endocarditis is suspected and clutter fills the aortic root. What is correct?

o.en: Lower near gain and sweep slowly through the root

why.en: Near field clutter can hide a root abscess, so optimise gain and sweep slowly before judging.
